\section[bēre]{\kn{ಬೇರೆ} (bēre) — other, different}

\label{lesson:KA-C102-other}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for please call, then the Kannada for urgent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬೇರೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬೇರೆ}} (\emph{bēre}) — \textquotedblleft{}other, different\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಬೇರೆ} \kn{ಬೇಕು}} (\emph{bēre bēku}) — \textquotedblleft{}I want a different one\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
When the first choice is wrong.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bēre}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bēre}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bēre bēku}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for please call, then the Kannada for urgent, then say \emph{bēre} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಬೇರೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Other, different\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tappu]{\kn{ತಪ್ಪು} (tappu) — wrong; a mistake}

\label{lesson:KA-C102-wrong}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for urgent, then the Kannada for other.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತಪ್ಪು}}
\textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪು}} (\emph{tappu}) — \textquotedblleft{}wrong\textquotedblright{}, and also \textquotedblleft{}a mistake\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪು} \kn{ಆಯ್ತು}} (\emph{tappu āytu}) — \textquotedblleft{}I made a mistake\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}a mistake happened\textquotedblright{}. It is the honest partner of \textbf{\kn{ಸರಿ}} (\emph{sari}), \textquotedblleft{}right\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The opposite of sari.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tappu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tappu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{tappu āytu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for urgent, then the Kannada for other, then say \emph{tappu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತಪ್ಪು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Wrong; a mistake\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಒಂದೇ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಒಂದೇ}} (\emph{ondē}) — \textquotedblleft{}only one\textquotedblright{}, or \textquotedblleft{}one and the same\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\kn{ಒಂದು}}, \textquotedblleft{}one\textquotedblright{}, with the emphatic \textbf{‑\kn{ಏ}} of \textbf{\kn{ಅದೇ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One, made emphatic.

\section[summane]{\kn{ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ} (summane) — for no reason, idly}

\label{lesson:KA-C102-fornoreason}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for all, then the Kannada for only one.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ}} (\emph{summane}) — \textquotedblleft{}for no reason, idly, quietly\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ}} answers \textbf{\kn{ಯಾಕೆ}?}, \textquotedblleft{}why?\textquotedblright{}, when there is no reason at all.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The answer to why when there is none.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{summane}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{summane}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for all, then the Kannada for only one, then say \emph{summane} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
